skill.name: global-validation
skill.description: Guides implementation of server-side validation, allowlists, type checks, input sanitization, and user-facing validation errors across entry points.
skill.summary: Guide AI coding agents to implement consistent validation for secure user input handling.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The two static findings were determined to be false positives. The path traversal pattern appears only in a fixed Markdown reference, not executable file access. The system reconnaissance alert is a business-rule validation example and shows no system inspection behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - When validating business rules (sufficient balance, valid dates, etc.)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 29 contains a hardcoded Markdown link to a standards document, not executable file access or user-controlled path handling. I found no evidence of arbitrary filesystem reads or path traversal behavior.
Line 16 describes business-rule validation examples such as balances and dates. It does not instruct the agent to inspect the host system or gather environment details.

content.value_statement: Input validation often becomes inconsistent across forms, APIs, and business rules. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward secure validation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Guides server-side validation for forms, APIs, and external input.
Promotes allowlist checks for accepted values, formats, and ranges.
Encourages type checking and required-field validation before business logic.
Covers input sanitization for SQL, XSS, and command injection prevention.
Supports consistent validation errors for clear user feedback.
Distinguishes security validation from client-side user experience checks.
limitations: Does not include the referenced detailed validation standard inside the packaged skill.
Does not provide framework-specific validation library code by itself.
Requires project context to choose exact schemas, rules, and error formats.
Does not replace security testing or penetration testing.

use_cases.title: Secure API Requests
use_cases.description: Define validation checks for request parameters and payloads before endpoint logic runs.

use_cases.title: Improve Form Validation
use_cases.description: Align client-side feedback with server-side enforcement for form submissions.

use_cases.title: Review Validation Coverage
use_cases.description: Check whether validation is applied consistently across entry points and business rules.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Validation Needs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature and list every input that needs validation. Separate security checks from user experience checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a form or API change.

prompt_templates.title: Design Validation Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create validation rules for these fields. Include required fields, type checks, ranges, formats, allowlists, and user-facing errors.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Consistent Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this code so validation runs server-side before business logic. Keep client-side validation for immediate feedback only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation across frontend and backend paths.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Validation Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this workflow for missing validation, unsafe input handling, weak sanitization, and inconsistent error behavior across entry points.

output_examples.input: A payment endpoint accepts amount, currency, and account identifier.
output_examples.output: Validate amount as a positive decimal within allowed limits. Allowlist supported currencies. Verify account identifier format before balance checks.

output_examples.input: A signup form validates email only in the browser.
output_examples.output: Move email format and required-field checks to the server. Keep browser validation for faster feedback, but do not trust it.

output_examples.input: A search field is passed into a database query.
output_examples.output: Limit length, normalize expected characters, and use safe query parameters. Return a clear validation error for unsupported input.

best_practices: Validate on the server before business logic or persistence.
Use allowlists for formats, ranges, enum values, and accepted identifiers.
Keep validation errors clear without exposing internal implementation details.
anti_patterns: Relying on client-side validation as the only enforcement layer.
Using blocklists as the main defense against malicious input.
Returning raw parser, database, or stack errors to users.

faq.question: Does this skill write validation code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the agent toward validation patterns. The final implementation depends on the project language, framework, and existing conventions.

faq.question: Should I still use client-side validation?
faq.answer: Yes. Client-side validation improves feedback, but server-side validation must enforce security and data integrity.

faq.question: What validation style does it recommend?
faq.answer: It favors allowlists, explicit type checks, required-field checks, range limits, format checks, and controlled error messages.

faq.question: Can it help with API validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports request parameter, payload, format, range, and business-rule validation for API endpoints.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It improves implementation guidance, but security review and testing are still required for sensitive workflows.

faq.question: Why is server-side validation emphasized?
faq.answer: Server-side validation protects every entry point, including direct API calls and clients that bypass browser checks.
